name: Sofia's eyes adjusting to a dark theatre

parameters.label: Minutes in the dark
parameters.explain: Full dark adaptation takes about 20–30 minutes: a quick first step in the first few minutes, then a bigger, slower one.

parameters.label: How bright it was before
parameters.explain: How long the eyes take to adjust depends on how bright the place you came from was.

parameters.label: Pupils
parameters.explain: Tests the 'only her pupils' idea. A fully open pupil lets in only about 16 times more light — far too little to explain everything.

overlay.caption: pupils open in seconds · light-sensing cells rebuild their pigment over minutes

explain.summary: Bright light uses up the light-sensing pigment in the cells at the back of the eye. When Sofia walks into the dark theatre, two things happen: her pupils open wide within seconds, letting in more light, and over many minutes her eye cells rebuild their pigment, becoming thousands of times more sensitive. The pupils help a little; the rebuilt pigment does most of the work.
rules: Pupils open from about 2.5 mm to 7.5 mm within seconds of entering the dark.
The eye's sensitivity starts far below its best and closes the gap by half about every 4 minutes.
The brighter the lobby and the longer she was in it, the bigger the gap at the start.
What she can see depends on her sensitivity, her pupils and how dark the theatre is.

source.fact: A normal pupil is 2–4 mm wide in bright light and 4–8 mm in dim light; in the dark, pupils get larger to let more light in.

The pupil can only enlarge its area about 16 times, yet we can see across changes in light level of far more than a million times. Cones max out after about five minutes; rods take over after about 10 minutes and do their best after about 20.
Complete dark adaptation takes about 30 minutes: an early increase over about 7 minutes from the cones, then a much greater one from the rods.
Dark adaptation usually takes 20–30 minutes to reach its maximum, depends on how bright the previous surroundings were, and works by regenerating the light-sensing pigment (rhodopsin in rods).

choice.what: Sensitivity is counted in 'log units' and its gap halves every 4 minutes
choice.why: Real dark adaptation has a fast cone step and a slower rod step; one smooth halving curve keeps the main idea and reaches nearly full sensitivity in about 20 minutes.

choice.what: Fully open pupils add 1.2 log units (about 16 times more light)
choice.why: This matches the 16-fold change in pupil area.

choice.what: Pupils finish opening in a few seconds
choice.why: Sources say the pupil opens almost immediately; we gave it a half-time of 2 seconds.

choice.what: Time in the lobby counts up to 10 minutes
choice.why: After that the pigment is treated as fully used up; the real relationship is more gradual.

illustrative: Sofia is fictional; the 'how much she can see' percentage is a made-up scale.
The 4-log-unit starting gap and the ×5,000 retina gain after 15 minutes are picked inside real ranges, not measured.

citations.title: Dilated Pupils (Mydriasis)
citations.supports: A pupil's normal size is 2–4 mm in bright light and 4–8 mm in dim light; in the dark, pupils get larger to allow more light in.

citations.title: How do my eyes adjust to the dark, and how long does it take?
citations.supports: The pupil can enlarge its area only about 16 times, but we see across light changes of far more than a million times; cones max out after about five minutes, rods take over after about 10 and do their best after about 20.

citations.title: Dark adaptation (e-Psych: the eye)
citations.supports: Complete dark adaptation takes about 30 minutes: an initial cone increase over about 7 minutes, then a much greater rod increase that is through in about half an hour.

citations.title: Why does it take so long for our vision to adjust to a darkened theater?
citations.supports: Dark adaptation typically takes 20–30 minutes to reach its maximum, depending on how bright the previous surroundings were; it restores sensitivity by regenerating rhodopsin and the cone pigments.

does: Shows pupils opening in seconds but giving only a small boost
Shows the eye's own sensitivity rising over many minutes as pigment is rebuilt
Shows a brighter lobby making the adjustment take longer
doesnt: Measure any real person — Sofia is fictional and the numbers are illustrative
Separate the cone step from the rod step, or show colour vision fading in the dark
Include age, screens, or eye conditions
limits.text: This is a simplified learning model. Real people vary with age, fitness and health. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements of any real person.
limits.wellbeing: If you notice you can't see well in dim light when your friends can, tell an adult — it's worth an eye check.
